_README: Which surveys are clean enough to be read in a report, round by round.
This is not approval and nothing in it is final. It records that the
reviewer has looked at the map and judged the data clean enough to put
in front of the clan, so the clan can correct it, answer the questions
on it, or go back and remap the gaps. The clan decides what their
There will be several rounds. Each survey holds a list under 'rounds',
oldest first, and a round is never overwritten: what went to the clan
in round 1 must still be readable after round 2 changes it. Add a new
Per round: 'round' the number, 'ready' the date, 'why' the reviewer's
reasoning, 'lines_only' for a survey going in as the recordings alone
with no polygon or area, 'withhold_area' where the computed area must
not be printed, and 'map' the file that went out, which is kept under
its round number so it is not overwritten.

captioned 'deari clain boundry maping'; the other four are
captioned 'nui clain boundry maping' by Patrick Dirise and Anthony
Irimari. Four stewards, one line, two clan names on it.

Three repairs stand behind it, each approved for this survey alone
and recorded in approved_fixes.json and line_extensions.json:
collapse_duplicates, because 93 recorded parts carry only 31
distinct; enclose_walked_land, for the 13.1 ha the reviewer found
encircled by Dickson Hoe's own tracks and falling outside; and the
node at 652677.8 652677.8E 8984946.2N where two of Stafford
Gidiri's stretches cross without either having an end there.
It has no stored boundary. The line came from the solver with those
fixes, not from the stored-segment model.

The question for the clan is the detached 727 m western loop that
s2 and s10 bracket: is that ground Ambunkol's? The answer decides
what those two stretches are. Nobody is sent to walk them first.
In the report, because going back to the clan is via the report.
The survey carries its question rather than being held back from
the clan who need to answer it.
NO AREA IS TO BE ISSUED. The pipeline closes the boundary using
Graham Ekiawa's sacred-site line as the northern edge and discards
5.4 km of the walked land boundary; that figure, 338 ha, must not
appear.
THE QUESTION FOR THE CLAN: where does the boundary run across the
north? Either the 20 July line titled 'Mungaikol Clan Sacred site
boundary' is the land boundary, leaving 3.2 km unwalked, or it is
what he titled it and the unwalked stretch is the 4.0 km across the
north. The two readings differ by about a third of the clan's land.
Graham is from the clan, so it goes to the clan with the map.

reviewer judged the area too confused to read, and it is not
settled either way. It goes to the clan as a question.
